{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development and Hosting Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the HDI Site Development and Hosting Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The draft is materially thin on risk allocation: it contains **no indemnification, no IP ownership provision, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no insurance covenant and no exit/transition mechanic**. HDI develops, hosts and operates the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, so these omissions leave us fully exposed at law and without any right to the work product or our own data.

The provisions that do exist skew against us in four places: (i) Section 6.1 imposes exclusive dealing and an open-ended non-compete on the Company for a term that renews indefinitely, with no performance-based exit; (ii) Section 4.2(a) imposes a Company-payable Termination Payment (half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, over eight quarters) that is untethered from our fees; (iii) Section 4.1 gives us at best a non-renewal right on 90 days' notice and does not confine HDI's exit to the end of a term; and (iv) Section 10.3 is a bare successors clause that would let HDI assign the hosting Agreement freely, including to a competitor.

Several items are compliant and require no redline: no Customer MFN, no minimum purchase or volume commitment, and no non-solicitation covenant binding the Company. New York governing law (Section 10.5) is our preferred law; only the venue sentence is missing. The Section 3.4 inspection right already exceeds the fallback on notice and cost and needs only a frequency cap.

Two findings were auto-repaired during verification (T4C, WARRANTY) and one failed verification and is not yet cleared for issue (RENEWAL, Section 4.1) — see Next steps.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; Section 9 is limited to authority reps and the Globix carve-out. We insert the preferred HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with claim procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity for our Content and breach of law, at the end of Section 9. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT | No IP ownership provision at all. Section 5.2 gives only artistic/editorial control, 5.3 covers physical product title, 6.1 is a trademark licence to HDI. We insert ownership of the Site and work product with assignment, a licence-back for embedded HDI IP, Company Data rights and no joint ownership. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause: no consent, no notice, no restriction on HDI, so HDI could assign to a competitor. Fails the fallback. We add Company freedom to assign to affiliates/successors, HDI assignment only with our consent and never to a competitor, and no HDI termination right on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 6.1 bars the Company from any similar Internet project for the whole term, and Section 4.1 renews that term annually and indefinitely, with no performance exit (Section 1.6 is a one-off 70-day go-live right). Walk-away territory. We cap the restriction at 12 months and end it automatically on HDI performance failure. HDI's own restrictions (6.3) benefit us and are not flagged. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 4.2 Termination Payment (half of the excess of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments) is Customer-payable, untethered from our 30%-of-Net-Sales fees and can far exceed three months' fees, failing the fallback cap. We zero out the formula while preserving the defined term so the "if any" mechanics in 4.2(b)–(c) stay consistent. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 6.1 extends to "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and "companies similar to" two named retailers — open-ended scope, fails the fallback. Only carve-out is the closeout site (6.2); no internal development or acquisition carve-out; term renews annually. We delete the Company covenant, leaving HDI's "Deerskin" brand exclusivity and Section 6.2 intact; fallback narrowing offered in comment. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Both exits sit inside the Section 4.1 auto-renewal sentence, so we have no express convenience right and HDI's exit is not confined to end of term. We add a standalone Company convenience right on 90 days' notice, limit HDI to end-of-term exit on the same notice, and cap the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 payments. Targeting fallback: notice stays at 90 days, no prepaid-fee refund pressed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 3.4 already exceeds the fallback on notice (30 days) and cost (HDI bears all fees unconditionally) and is limited to business hours and payment records, but has no frequency limit — failing the fallback and approaching the walk-away "unlimited audits". Single minimal edit: cap inspections at once per year. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 10.5 selects New York law (our preferred), and there is no arbitration clause or foreign venue. However there is no dispute forum provision at all. We add only the missing exclusive New York County venue sentence after Section 10.5. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 1.4 grants the Company access to and use of the hosting system, HDI software and Content tools; it is not revocable at will and Section 10.3 covers successors, so the transfer element is met. It names only "the Company" with no affiliate path, failing that fallback element. We add one sentence extending access and use to our affiliates on written notice. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No Customer MFN. Sections 3.1–3.4 fix a flat 30% of Net Sales with no obligation to extend or match third-party terms; the only "no less favorably" covenant (§ 1.8) runs against HDI and § 7.1 is reciprocal. Meets the preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No minimum purchase, spend, volume or take-or-pay obligation. HDI is paid only on actual Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold (which operates in our favour), reconciled quarterly. Preferred position. The § 4.2 Termination Payment is an exit charge and is addressed under LD/T4C. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere; the only restrictive covenants are Section 6 exclusivity and Section 8 confidentiality. Section 10.7 integration prevents any imported personnel covenant. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Needs review *(verification: fail)* | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 4.1 renews for one-year terms (acceptable) but the only exit is 90 days' written notice, failing the 60-day fallback ceiling. No renewal uplift right exists (fees are a 30% revenue share), so the price-cap element is not triggered. Proposed edit replaces the 90-day period with 60 days' prior written notice, retaining the mutual right, one-year term and "Termination Date" definition. **Edit failed verification — hold pending manual redraft.** |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 4 covers only term, notice and the Termination Payment. Nothing requires HDI to assist on transition or to return, export or delete our Content, user information or order data on exit, despite HDI holding all of it. Fails even the fallback. We insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred position. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 9 warrants only corporate existence, authority, enforceability and non-conflict (9(a)) plus the Globix acknowledgment (9(b)). No conformity or performance warranty, duration or remedy — the fallback fails on all four material terms. No "AS IS" clause, so no carve-out needed. We insert Section 9(c): 12 months for Site/software conformity to documentation, 90 days for services, with repair, replacement or refund of fees paid. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No insurance covenant anywhere; Sections 10.1–10.8 run from notices to headings. HDI hosts the Site, processes order export files and accesses user and customer data (§§ 1.4, 1.5, 8.1), so the absence of coverage for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory. We insert Section 10.9 at preferred levels (CGL $1M/$2M, E&O $2M, cyber $5M, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request). |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No liability cap, damages exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere; Sections 8, 9 and 10.1–10.8 contain none. Both parties are fully exposed at law. We insert the fallback as a new Section 10.9: mutual cap at twelve months' fees, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the findings our rationales identify as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on them:

1. **No HDI indemnity (INDEMN, § 9 / General Provisions).** The complete absence of an indemnity for third-party IP infringement arising from the Site development and hosting work, and for HDI's own misconduct, is walk-away under the playbook.
2. **Company exclusivity with no performance exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 6.1 with § 4.1).** Exclusive dealing for the full term, on a term that auto-renews annually and indefinitely, with no automatic exit for HDI non-performance.
3. **No insurance where HDI processes personal data (INSURANCE, §§ 10.1–10.8).** HDI hosts the Site and handles user, customer and order data with no coverage obligation at all.

**Approaching walk-away:** the Section 3.4 inspection right has no frequency limit and so approaches the "unlimited audits" walk-away; the single once-per-year cap resolves it.

**Also high-priority, though not walk-away as drafted:** the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment (LD/T4C), the open-ended Section 6.1 non-compete scope (NONCOMPETE), the unrestricted HDI assignment right (ASSIGN), the missing IP ownership provision (IP), and the absence of any liability cap (LOL-CAP).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the failed edit.** The RENEWAL finding (Section 4.1, 90-day notice window) failed verification and is marked needs review. We will manually redraft the 60-day non-recurring notice sentence before the markup goes out, taking care not to disturb the mutual either-Party right, the one-year renewal term, the anniversary mechanic or the "Termination Date" definition.
2. **Confirm the two repaired edits.** Re-read the T4C insertion at Section 4.1/4.2(a) and the new Section 9(c) warranty in context to confirm the repaired language reads cleanly and does not conflict with the Section 4.2 changes made under LD.
3. **De-conflict the two new Section 10.9 inserts.** INSURANCE and LOL-CAP both propose a new Section 10.9; we will renumber so insurance and limitation of liability sit as separate, sequential clauses.
4. **Sequence Section 4.2.** The LD redline zeroes the Termination Payment formula while T4C caps it at three months' fees. We will lead with the LD position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and hold the three-month cap as the stated fallback.
5. **Issue the markup** with [Playbook] comments on each redline, noting where we sit at the fallback (LICENSE affiliates, WARRANTY, LOL-CAP, T4C notice period) and where we are at preferred (INDEMN, IP, ASSIGN, TRANSITION, GOVLAW venue, INSURANCE).
6. **Escalate the three walk-away items** to the business owner before the next negotiation session, so we have authority on the exclusivity term and the insurance floors.
7. **No action** on MFN, MINCOMMIT and NOSOLICIT — compliant at the preferred position.
"}
